+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Controlled CPU/CUDA agreement, with no high-resolution runs."""
+import csv
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+import numpy as np
+
+HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT=HERE.parents[1]
+OUT=HERE/"validation"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+
+def config(name,backend,options):
+    d=dict(nr=12,ntheta=4,nphi=12,rmin_au=.1,rmax_au=2.3,latmax_deg=30,
+           radial_grid="uniform",gamma=1.5,cfl=.35,order=2,threads=1,
+           start_day=0,end_day=.2,snapshot_days=.1,output_dir=OUT/f"{name}_{backend}")
+    d.update(options)
+    path=OUT/f"{name}_{backend}.cfg"
+    path.write_text("".join(f"{k}={v}\n" for k,v in d.items()))
+    return path,d
+
+
+def run(name,options):
+    folders={}
+    for backend in ["cpu","gpu"]:
+        path,opts=config(name,backend,options)
+        # An explicit output_dir override applies only to the named case, so
+        # always isolate the two backends even if input options were copied.
+        opts["output_dir"]=OUT/f"{name}_{backend}"
+        path.write_text("".join(f"{k}={v}\n" for k,v in opts.items()))
+        if backend=="gpu":exe=HERE/"mhd_cuda"
+        else:exe=ROOT/"solver/induction_cpu"/("mhd_solver_inductive_split" if opts.get("flux_variant")=="split_llf" else "mhd_solver_inductive")
+        subprocess.run([str(exe),"--config",str(path)],check=True,timeout=300)
+        folders[backend]=Path(opts["output_dir"])
+    a=np.load(sorted(folders["cpu"].glob("snapshot_*.npy"))[-1]).astype(float)
+    b=np.load(sorted(folders["gpu"].glob("snapshot_*.npy"))[-1]).astype(float)
+    scale=np.max(abs(a),axis=(0,1,2))
+    relative=abs(b-a)/(abs(a)+1e-6*scale+1e-12)
+    metric=dict(maximum_snapshot_scaled_difference=float(np.max(relative)),
+                maximum_absolute_difference_by_field=np.max(abs(a-b),axis=(0,1,2)).tolist(),
+                cpu_statistics=json.loads((folders['cpu']/'statistics.json').read_text()),
+                gpu_statistics=json.loads((folders['gpu']/'statistics.json').read_text()))
+    probe=folders["cpu"]/"probe.csv"
+    if probe.exists() and len(probe.read_text().splitlines())>1:
+        p=np.genfromtxt(probe,delimiter=",",names=True)
+        q=np.genfromtxt(folders["gpu"]/"probe.csv",delimiter=",",names=True)
+        metric["maximum_probe_relative_difference"]={name:float(np.max(abs(q[name]-p[name])/(abs(p[name])+1e-30))) for name in ["n_cm3","speed_kms","flux_cm2_s"]}
+    (OUT/f"{name}_agreement.json").write_text(json.dumps(metric,indent=2)+"\n")
+    print(name,json.dumps(metric),flush=True)
+    assert metric["maximum_snapshot_scaled_difference"]<1e-4,metric
+    if "maximum_probe_relative_difference" in metric:
+        assert max(metric["maximum_probe_relative_difference"].values())<1e-5,metric
+    return metric
+
+
+if __name__=="__main__":
+    cases={
+        "uniform":dict(nr=8,ntheta=4,nphi=8,gravity_gm=0,test_cartesian_uniform=1),
+        "radial":dict(),
+        "real_tiny":dict(boundary_map_csv=ROOT/"inputs/boundary_map.csv",start_day=9,end_day=9.2,map_rotation_rad_day=.24756448241988369,map_longitude_offset_rad=-1.0502672621698068),
+    }
+    file=OUT/"synthetic_inductive.csv"
+    with file.open("w",newline="") as f:
+        writer=csv.writer(f);writer.writerow(["day","lon_rad","lat_rad","speed_kms","density_1au_cm3","br_1au_nt","temperature_K","emf_theta_nT_AU_day","emf_phi_nT_AU_day"])
+        for t in [0,.1,.2]:
+            for lat in [-.5,0,.5]:
+                for lon in np.arange(8)*2*np.pi/8:
+                    writer.writerow([t,lon,lat,420+40*np.cos(lon),5,3*np.cos(lon),2e5,.1*np.sin(lon)*(1+t),.1*np.cos(lon)*(1+t)])
+    probe=OUT/"synthetic_probes.csv"
+    with probe.open("w",newline="") as f:
+        writer=csv.writer(f);writer.writerow(["day","r_au","lon_rad","lat_rad","probe_id"])
+        for t in np.arange(7)*.05:writer.writerow([t,.8,1.2,.1,0])
+    cases["inductive_global"]=dict(boundary_map_csv=file,probes_csv=probe,end_day=.3,snapshot_days=.05,outer_magnetic_radial_scaling=1)
+    cases["inductive_split"]={**cases["inductive_global"],"flux_variant":"split_llf"}
+    names=sys.argv[1:] or list(cases)
+    results={name:run(name,cases[name]) for name in names}
+    (OUT/"agreement_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+"\n")
*** End Patch"));

+This is a controlled CUDA float64 port of the spherical finite-volume solver,
+not a separate physical model. The original CPU source and executable remain
+unchanged. Build with `make` in this directory, then run
+`./mhd_cuda --config /absolute/path/run.cfg`. CUDA 12 and an sm_89 GPU are the
+current tested build targets; override NVCCFLAGS for another architecture.
+
+The key/value configuration and outputs follow `../README.md`. Additional
+configuration is `flux_variant=global_llf` (original global GLM-speed Rusanov)
+or `flux_variant=split_llf` (exact normal-B/q GLM interface preprocessing,
+local fast-magnetosonic Rusanov for the remaining MHD variables). These select
+the same two controlled CPU reference variants in `../induction_cpu/`.
+Neither choice represents a constrained-transport algorithm.
+
+All evolution arithmetic, conserved states, reconstructed primitives, geometry,
+and boundary interpolation use double precision. Fused multiply-add is disabled
+to make the CPU comparison strict. Geometry, initial conditions, angular basis
+vectors, and configuration are computed by a frozen host copy of the CPU
+reference. Conserved states, fluxes, RK stages, and boundary maps then remain on
+the GPU. Only reduced scalar diagnostics, requested probes, and snapshots cross
+the device boundary. Snapshot output retains the CPU float32 NumPy format;
+probe output retains its 12-digit CSV precision.
+
+The optional boundary CSV columns `emf_theta_nT_AU_day` and
+`emf_phi_nT_AU_day` are angularly interpolated and taken from the left time
+interval. Their value is zero before the first map and at or after the final
+map. Other primitive map quantities retain linear interpolation in time.
+The boundary adds Btheta=-Ephi/vr and Bphi=Etheta/vr to the rotating Parker
+field, with the same r0/r initialization scaling as the controlled CPU source.
+This center-sampled electric-field interpolation is an approximation to the
+external discrete surface closure; it does not impose that staggered closure
+exactly on this finite-volume mesh.
+
+`outer_magnetic_radial_scaling=1` extrapolates Br proportional to r^-2 and
+tangential B proportional to r^-1 in the outer ghost layers. Its default is
+zero. The density, pressure, velocity, and cleaning variable are copied there,
+matching the controlled CPU reference.
+
+The SSPRK2, GLM energy/damping, strict positivity checks, global first-order
+fallback and timestep-halving logic follow the CPU reference. There are no
+positivity floors. Statistics report rejected attempts and fallback steps.
+Each directional flux, update, reduction, and ghost operation uses a separate
+kernel. The program does not request exclusive GPU mode or change device power
+settings. Only one instance should run at a time under the shared GPU runner.
+
+All device allocations are tracked and hard-capped at 2.3 GB, leaving roughly
+200 MB within the 2.5 GB agreed budget for runtime/context overhead. A preflight
+check requires another 500 MB free beyond the estimated arrays. Host allocation
+omits all CPU stepping work arrays: it keeps only initial/output u and p plus
+geometry, approximately 248 bytes per ghost-extended cell. The runner should
+monitor resident host and device memory and enforce its wall-time budget;
+RLIMIT_AS is unsuitable for CUDA's large virtual address reservation.
+
+`python validate.py` executes controlled CPU/CUDA tests, writes isolated inputs
+and results under `validation/`, and compares final fields and probe outputs.
+`reference_provenance.json` pins the source and header hashes.
+`freeze_host_reference.py` regenerates that header only when explicitly invoked
+after source review; `make` never silently refreshes it. Regeneration requires
+repeating the CPU/CUDA agreement checks before production refinement.
